C0.quote: selecting a fixed-size subset of candidates (a so-called committee) based on the approval preferences
C0.note: Approval-based committee voting rules; axiomatic, complexity and experimental analysis.

C1.quote: we formalize the concept of individual representation (IR) and explore to which extent
C1.note: AX: IR, incompatibilities, rule failures, domain bounds. AL: NP-hardness, algorithm for VI. SI: experiments on generated profiles. Primary AX by share of results.

C2.1.quote: An (approval) profile A = (A1 , . . . , An ) contains the approval set Ai

C2.2.quote: Domain restrictions for dichotomous (i.e., approval) preferences have been studied
C2.2.note: Approval sets; the paper also calls them dichotomous preferences.

C2.3.quote: based on the approval preferences of voters
C2.3.note: Approval preferences, opinions, and voters' evaluation of committees are referred to; the approval set is both input and preference.

C2.4.quote: Each voter i ∈ N approves a subset Ai ⊆ C of candidates.
C2.4.note: Approval sets are described as voters' preferences and the rules are applied directly, with no statement about submission or misreporting.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.quote: voter i evaluates a committee W by |W ∩ Ai |
C4.1.note: Satisfaction is tied to the approval count, which is a stated relation; the paper also says IR is 'fair' to voters. Not formally framed as utility from ranking. SPEC could arguably fit; chose PART because satisfaction is only used as a standard assumption and not formally defined.

C4.2.note: The term is used as a synonym for approval; the two classes are not described in terms of utility or a richer preference.

C5.1.note: IR, EJR, PJR and core stability are representation and proportionality criteria used in formal results and experiments.

C5.2.quote: |W ∩ Ai | ≥ f i for all voters i ∈ N
C5.2.note: Representation is evaluated on approval sets, with no statement relating them to held attitudes.

VOT.note: Voters only supply approval sets and take no action in the model.

claims.quote: our goal is to provide all members of a voter group equal guarantees
common voting rules sometimes unfairly distinguish between such voters
IR is achievable in many instances that follow somewhat realistic preferences

C9.1.note: Claims about fairness to voters and realistic achievability.

C9.2.quote: common voting rules sometimes unfairly distinguish between such voters
C9.2.note: The fairness-to-voters claim needs a statement that approval sets equal voters' held preferences, which is not stated. The 'realistic preferences' claim needs the generated data to be realistic, which is only partly addressed.
